case_title: Kashibai & Ors. v. The State of Karnataka
accused_victim_relationship: Spouse (accused no.3 was the victim's husband); parents-in-law (accused nos.1 and 2)
statutory_provisions: IPC s.498A r/w s.34; IPC s.306 r/w s.34 (acquitted on appeal)
evidence_type: Oral testimony of family and neighbours on dowry harassment; medical (post-mortem) evidence; documentary evidence; hostile witnesses
aggravating_circumstances: Alleged and accepted for s.498A: physical and mental harassment of the victim over dowry demands for cash and gold
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.498A r/w s.34 (2 years SI, Rs 2,000 fine each) and s.306 r/w s.34 (5 years SI, Rs 5,000 fine each); accused no.4 acquitted
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed; conviction and sentence confirmed
neutral_facts: The victim married one of the accused about three years before the incident. The victim's mother complained to police that, after the marriage, the victim's husband, parents-in-law and brother-in-law ill-treated the victim physically and mentally over demands for dowry in cash and gold. The complaint stated that the victim died by jumping into an open well in a field in a village on a morning in February 2010. Twenty-one witnesses and documentary evidence were presented at trial. The victim's parents, an uncle, a person who arranged the marriage and two neighbours testified about dowry demands and harassment of the victim by the accused. Four witnesses turned hostile. The post-mortem doctor recorded the cause of death as drowning due to asphyxia, but gave no opinion on whether the death was suicidal or accidental. The victim's mother first alleged that the victim had been thrown into the well, later admitting she had not seen the body there. She also said one accused had told her by telephone that the victim had accidentally slipped. Other witnesses did not know whether the victim had jumped or slipped. When the body was taken out of the well, all four accused were present near the well.
offence_severity: Not stated for s.498A. For s.306 (acquitted): imprisonment up to ten years and fine; no minimum stated
physical_harm: Death of the victim by drowning due to asphyxia; the post-mortem report recorded injuries on the body but the court did not find whether the death was suicidal
motive: Dowry demands for cash and gold, with resulting physical and mental harassment; the court accepted the harassment for s.498A but found no proven abetment of suicide
key_evidence_accepted: Testimony of parents, uncle, marriage arranger and neighbours on dowry demands and harassment (accepted for s.498A); post-mortem report on drowning due to asphyxia; no evidence accepted showing abetment of suicide
witness_credibility: Harassment evidence from parents, uncle, marriage arranger and neighbours was accepted as establishing s.498A. Four witnesses turned hostile. The mother admitted not seeing the body and not stating suicide in her complaint; the father, marriage arranger and uncle had no knowledge of how the victim fell into the well. The court gave no credit to any evidence of abetment.
post_offence_conduct: As recounted by the mother, accused no.3 telephoned her saying the victim had accidentally slipped into the well; the court did not treat this as a finding
custody_duration: Served two years of imprisonment under s.498A r/w s.34; exact custody period not stated
trial_duration: offence: 07.02.2010; trial judgment: 11.02.2014; High Court: 06.03.2021; Supreme Court: 28.02.2023 (judgment date; hearing date not given)
legal_representation: Appellants (accused): Ms. Afshan Pracha, Prakash Jadhav, Anirudh Sanganeria, Ravichandra Jadhav. State/respondent: Shubhranshu Padhi, Vishal Bansal, Ms. Rajeshwari Shankar, Niroop Sukirthy, Md. Ovais
investigation_status: Complaint registered at Bableshwar Police Station under ss.498A and 306 r/w 304 IPC; trial completed with 21 prosecution witnesses
appeal_history: Trial court (II Additional Sessions Judge, Bijapur, 11.02.2014): convicted under ss.498A and 306 r/w 34. High Court (06.03.2021): appeal dismissed. Supreme Court: appeal partly allowed; s.498A conviction upheld, s.306 conviction set aside
legal_principle_applied: To convict under s.306 IPC, the death must be suicidal and abetment under s.107 must be proved, requiring evidence of instigation, conspiracy or intentional aid and a positive act by the accused. The s.113A Evidence Act presumption is discretionary and is not raised merely by a suicide within seven years of marriage.
precedent_relied_upon: M. Mohan v. State Represented by the Deputy Superintendent of Police (2011) 3 SCC 626; Mangat Ram v. State of Haryana (2014) 12 SCC 595
sentencing_rationale: Appellants had already served the two-year sentence for s.498A r/w s.34, so they were set free forthwith
other_sentence_order: Appellants directed to be set free forthwith
